info.name: UNBLOCK-AI API
info.description: Endpoints exposed by the Express server (src/app.ts, src/routes/). Generated to match docs/api/api-documentation.md. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner in folder order: Health, Auth, Users, Organisation, User affiliations, Workflow Templates, Task requests, Approver inbox, Approvals, Transcript, Error cases. Most requests need a bearer token - the collection-level auth reads it from {{authToken}}, captured by the 'Login' request in the Auth folder from {{loginEmail}} / {{loginPassword}}. Set loginEmail to the administrator seeded by 'npm run seed:pg:run' (SEED_ADMINISTRATOR_EMAIL) and loginPassword to the server's USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD. The Task requests, Approvals and Transcript folders run as {{requesterEmail}} (a seeded sample user, SEED_SAMPLE_USERS=true) through {{requesterToken}}. The Approver inbox folder decides the first approval in the app as the approver it finds on the task (through {{approverToken}}), with no email involved. The Approvals folder needs the next approval URL pasted by hand from the console mailer's stdout into {{approvalUrl}} after 'Submit form' -- it cannot be fully automated by the Collection Runner.

variable.value: I want to take 1 month overseas leave for a research visit. Guide me through the process.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns { status, uptime, version }.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Login stores the token in {{authToken}}, which the collection-level Bearer auth sends on every later request. Credentials come from {{loginEmail}} / {{loginPassword}} (the administrator seeded by npm run seed:pg:run, whose password is USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD). The session requests use a second, throwaway session so {{authToken}} is never revoked mid-run. See docs/api/api-documentation.md §12.

request.description: Logs in with {{loginEmail}} / {{loginPassword}} and stores the returned token in {{authToken}}. Set those two collection variables to the seeded administrator's SEED_ADMINISTRATOR_EMAIL and the server's USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD.

exec: pm.test("response has token, expires_at and user", function () { pm.expect(json).to.have.property("token"); pm.expect(json).to.have.property("expires_at"); pm.expect(json).to.have.property("user"); });

request.description: Confirms {{authToken}} is valid. Returns { user: { id, email, full_name, permissions }, session: { id, expires_at } }.

exec: pm.test("response has user and session", function () { pm.expect(json).to.have.property("user"); pm.expect(json).to.have.property("session"); });

request.description: Logs in again as the same user to open a second concurrent session. Its token goes into {{secondAuthToken}}, not {{authToken}}, so the requests below can revoke it safely.
The caller's active sessions, newest first. The session behind {{authToken}} has is_current: true. Stores the newest other session (the one from 'Login (second session)') in {{otherUserSessionId}}.

exec: pm.test("sessions is an array", function () { pm.expect(sessions).to.be.an("array"); });
pm.test("exactly one session is current", function () { pm.expect(sessions.filter(function (s) { return s.is_current; }).length).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Revokes one of the caller's own sessions by id (204). A session that is not one of the caller's active sessions is 404 USER_SESSION_NOT_FOUND; a non-UUID id is 400. Revoking the current session behaves like logout - do not point this at the session behind {{authToken}}.

exec: pm.test("revoked token is rejected with 401", function () { pm.expect(res.code).to.eql(401); });

request.description: Revokes every active session of the caller except the current one. Returns { revoked_count }. This also signs out any other browser or device logged in as the same user, such as the web app.

Revokes the session the request is made with (204). The pre-request script logs in a throwaway session into {{logoutToken}} and this request logs that one out, so {{authToken}} keeps working for the rest of the run. Calling logout with {{authToken}} itself would make every later request 401.

exec: if (err || res.code !== 200) { console.error("throwaway login failed", err || res.code); return; }
pm.test("logged-out token is rejected with 401", function () { pm.expect(res.code).to.eql(401); });

item.name: Users
item.description: User management. Every request needs the user:manage permission, which the seeded administrator holds. New users get USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD as their initial password. See docs/api/api-documentation.md §13.

request.description: Creates a user with only task:create. The email uses {{$timestamp}} so repeated runs do not hit 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED. permissions must be non-empty, known values, no duplicates. Stores user.id in {{userId}}.

exec: pm.test("user has the requested permissions", function () { pm.expect(user.permissions).to.eql(["task:create"]); });

request.description: Users one page at a time, ordered by full_name. Query: search, organisational_unit_id, limit (1-100, default 25), offset. Returns { users: UserListItemDto[], page: { total, limit, offset } }.

exec: pm.test("users is an array", function () { pm.expect(users).to.be.an("array"); });
pm.test("includes the created user", function () { pm.expect(users.map(function (u) { return u.id; })).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("userId")); });

request.description: One UserDto. 404 USER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 400 for a non-UUID id.

item.name: Organisation
item.description: Faculties, departments, divisions and designations. Reads need any session; writes need organisation:manage. The requests create a temporary faculty, department and designation and remove them again at the end of 'User affiliations'.

request.description: Every unit including archived ones. Filters: unit_type, parent_id, root_only, include_archived.
Creates a temporary faculty. Stores its id in {{facultyId}}.
A department must belong to a faculty. Stores its id in {{departmentId}}.
Rejected with ORGANISATIONAL_UNIT_PARENT_INVALID.
A single-holder designation for departments. Stores its id in {{designationId}}.

item.name: User affiliations
item.description: Assigns the temporary department and designation to {{userId}} (from Users › Create user), reads them back, then cleans up.

request.description: The body is the complete desired state. Returns { affiliations: UserAffiliationsDto }.

exec: pm.test("one membership with the designation", function () { pm.expect(affiliations.memberships[0].designations[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("designationId")); });
pm.test("the user is a member", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().members.map(function (m) { return m.user.id; })).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("userId")); });

request.description: Filtering by a faculty includes members of its departments.

exec: pm.test("the user is listed", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().users.map(function (u) { return u.id; })).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("userId")); });

item.name: Workflow Templates
item.description: Author a workflow template end to end: generate version 1 from a prompt, rename it and save prompt edits, publish it, regenerate (a published template stays published and the new version goes live immediately), read the version history, archive and restore it, and save a separate draft. workflowTemplateId is captured from 'Generate workflow template' and used by the rest of this folder and by Selection. The generate requests call the LLM and are slow (10-60s) - raise the Postman request timeout before running. The prompt is the text of src/data/samples/demo-drafts/workshop_event.txt, which matches the query used in the Selection folder.

request.description: Creates a template and generates version 1 in one call. title is optional; without it the model-generated title is used. Result status: unpublished. Slow (10-60s). 422 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_PROMPT_REJECTED if the prompt is not a workflow, 422 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_GENERATION_FAILED if no valid definition came back.

exec: pm.test("status is unpublished at version 1", function () { pm.expect(json.workflow_template.status).to.eql("unpublished"); pm.expect(json.workflow_template.current_version).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Non-archived templates, newest updated_at first, in the summary shape (no draft_prompt, no current).

exec: pm.test("includes the generated template", function () { pm.expect(json.workflow_templates.map(function (t) { return t.id; })).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("workflowTemplateId")); });

request.description: include_archived accepts only 'true' or 'false' (default false). There is no server-side status or search filter.
The template with its current version (prompt + definition) under current. Requires workflow:manage or task:create.

Both fields optional. A title change never creates a version. draft_prompt saves an edited prompt without generating (null discards it; not allowed on a draft). 409 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_ARCHIVED on an archived template.

exec: pm.test("title changed without a new version", function () { pm.expect(json.workflow_template.title).to.eql("Departmental Workshop & Event Approval"); pm.expect(String(json.workflow_template.current_version)).to.eql(String(pm.collectionVariables.get("templateVersion"))); });

request.description: No body. Makes the current version available to requesters through selection. 409 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_NOT_GENERATED on a draft, WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_ALREADY_PUBLISHED, or WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_ARCHIVED.

Generates version current_version + 1 from the prompt and clears draft_prompt. The template is already published, so it stays published and the new version is offered to requesters immediately; older versions stay stored for tasks pinned to them. Slow (10-60s).
Version history, newest first, without prompts or definitions.

One version with the prompt it was generated from and its definition. The stored definition has no title - the title lives on the template. 404 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND for an unknown version.

exec: pm.test("version has prompt and definition", function () { var v = pm.response.json().version; pm.expect(v).to.have.property("prompt"); pm.expect(v).to.have.property("definition"); });

request.description: No body. Archive replaces delete: the template keeps its status but is hidden from the default list, never offered by selection, and read-only until restored. Tasks already created from it keep running.
No body. The template returns with the status it had - here published, so Selection can find it again. 409 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_NOT_ARCHIVED if it is not archived.

Saves a title and prompt as a draft. Nothing is generated and no LLM call is made. Generate it later with POST /workflow-templates/:workflowTemplateId/generate. The id is captured into draftWorkflowTemplateId for the Error cases folder.

exec: pm.test("status is draft with no version", function () { pm.expect(json.workflow_template.status).to.eql("draft"); pm.expect(json.workflow_template.current).to.eql(null); });

item.name: Task requests
item.description: The requester journey: assistant conversation, task creation, form draft and submit. Runs as {{requesterEmail}} (default u17@u.c, Kavindu, a student in the Department of Information Technology seeded with SEED_SAMPLE_USERS=true), because selection depends on the caller's affiliations and tasks are visible only to their creator. Publish an IT overseas-leave template first (src/data/samples/demo-drafts/).

request.description: Logs in as {{requesterEmail}} with USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD and stores the token in {{requesterToken}}.
Published templates the requester is eligible for. No embedding and no LLM call.
First message. Reads the profile, embeds once, filters by eligibility and consults the selector (one LLM call when a candidate survives). Stores the session id in {{sessionId}}.

exec: pm.test("ends with an assistant message", function () { pm.expect(last.role).to.eql("assistant"); });
pm.test("assistant matched a template", function () { pm.expect(["matched", "start_requested"]).to.include(last.decision); });

request.description: Restores the conversation, as the web app does after a refresh.
Compiles and starts the task, and deletes the selection session. Stores {{taskId}}, the submittable form's id in {{formId}} and its fields in {{formFields}}.

form.sections.forEach(function (s) { s.fields.forEach(function (f) { fields.push({ id: f.id, control: f.control, locked: f.locked, validation: f.validation, options: f.options }); }); });

item.name: Approver inbox
item.description: Signed-in approver path (task:approve), no email involved. Finds who the task is waiting on, logs in as them into {{approverToken}}, then lists, opens and decides the approval in the app. Runs after Task requests: the entry form names {{advisorEmail}} (default the seeded Ishara Bandara, U6@U.C in mixed case on purpose) as the academic advisor, so the first approval is in her inbox. Every request sends {{approverToken}} unless it says otherwise.

request.description: Runs as the requester. Stores the email of the step that is awaiting_approver in {{approverEmail}}.

exec: pm.test("a step is awaiting an approver", function () { pm.expect(step).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(step.assignee.email).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: Logs in as {{approverEmail}} with USER_DEFAULT_PASSWORD and stores the token in {{approverToken}}.
Oldest first. Stores the step id of this task's row in {{approvalStepId}}.

exec: var row = json.approvals.find(function (a) { return a.task_id === pm.collectionVariables.get("taskId"); });
pm.test("task is pending for this approver", function () { pm.expect(row).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(row.decision).to.eql(null); });

request.description: The same comment rules as the emailed link.

Records decided_via: app and clears this step's emailed link. To try the information request loop instead, send {"decision": "request_more_info", "comment": "…"}; after the requester answers, the repeat review shows up in pending again.
Newest decision first, filtered to approvals.

exec: var row = pm.response.json().approvals.find(function (a) { return a.task_id === pm.collectionVariables.get("taskId") && a.step_id === pm.collectionVariables.get("approvalStepId"); });
pm.test("decision is in history", function () { pm.expect(row).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(row.decision).to.eql("approved"); pm.expect(row.decided_via).to.eql("app"); });

request.description: Runs as the requester, who holds task:create only.

item.name: Approvals
item.description: Approver path, no session. The Approver inbox folder has already decided the first approval in the app, so paste the URL of the NEXT approval email printed by the console mailer (MAIL_TRANSPORT=console) into the {{approvalUrl}} collection variable (a bare token also works). The folder's pre-request script extracts {{approvalToken}}. Repeat paste, view and approve for each remaining approval step. A link for a step already decided in the app shows decided.

request.description: A comment is required for rejected and request_more_info.

To try the information request loop instead, send {"decision": "request_more_info", "comment": "…"}; the task gains an information_request step whose form the requester submits (Task requests → Submit form after re-running Get task), and a new link is emailed to the same approver.

item.name: Transcript
item.description: Rendered on demand for a completed task, never stored. Runs as the requester. Cancel and delete clean up the task afterwards.

request.description: 200 application/pdf once every approval is done; 409 TASK_TRANSCRIPT_UNAVAILABLE before that.
Cancels open steps and revokes approval links. 409 TASK_NOT_ACTIVE once the task has finished.

item.name: Generate workflow template — not a workflow (422)

request.description: Expected: 422 WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_PROMPT_REJECTED with the model's reasons in details. The verdict comes from the LLM, so a model that invents a workflow anyway will fail this test. Slow (10-60s).

exec: pm.test("body has error and code", function () { pm.expect(json).to.have.property("error"); pm.expect(json).to.have.property("code"); });

item.name: Get selection session — used by a task (404)

request.description: Starting a task deletes its selection session.
Deliberately 404, not 401 or 500 — a malformed or unrecognised token does not confirm or deny that a token of that shape ever existed.
An unknown email gets the same 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS as a wrong password. Uses an unregistered email so it never counts toward any account's lockout.
